coverage_gaps: Only PubMed is available, so independent subject indexes, citation graphs, and DOI metadata services cannot verify citation expansion or discover non-PubMed records.

Trial registries, regulator databases, preprint servers, patent sources, and chemistry databases are unavailable; ongoing, regulatory, recent unreviewed, and prior-art evidence remains outside direct coverage.

Dedicated genetics resources such as GWAS catalogs, clinical-variant databases, population-frequency databases, and pedigree repositories are unavailable for independent variant classification and ancestry-frequency checks.
PubMed indexing and abstract availability may underrepresent non-English, very recent, conference-only, and poorly indexed studies.
Full-text access is outside the supplied route, which may limit assessment of assay details, cohort overlap, exact phosphosites, and nuanced negative findings.
exclusion_criteria: LRRK1-only studies without separable evidence about LRRK2.
Records that mention Parkinson disease or LRRK2 solely as background and provide no relevant genetic, enzymatic, substrate, physiological, or limiting evidence.
Pure docking, prediction, or overexpression-only substrate claims lacking direct phosphorylation evidence are excluded from the physiological-substrate evidence tier.
Drug efficacy or safety studies without interpretable evidence about LRRK2 genetics, target engagement, enzymatic mechanism, substrates, or mechanism-limiting outcomes.
Non-Parkinson disease studies without transferable LRRK2 enzymatic, substrate, tissue-context, or limitation evidence.
Editorials, news items, and unsourced opinions that add no traceable primary evidence.
Duplicate canonical records are merged by PMID, DOI, and title-year identity while every query-to-record occurrence is retained.
inclusion_criteria: Publication, online-first, or correction date is on or before 2024-12-31; ambiguous indexing dates are adjudicated after retrieval.
LRRK2 and Parkinson disease or parkinsonism are central to the genetic, mechanistic, physiological, or limiting evidence.
Primary human genetic studies report linkage, segregation, association, ancestry, penetrance, founder, pathogenic, risk, or protective evidence for named LRRK2 variants.
Mechanistic studies directly measure LRRK2 kinase, ROC-COR GTPase, GTP binding or hydrolysis, autophosphorylation, structure, or variant-dependent activity.

A physiological-substrate designation requires endogenous-site evidence plus LRRK2 genetic or pharmacological dependence in cells, tissue, organisms, or human material; weaker candidates remain eligible when explicitly labeled proposed.
Negative, null, contradictory, replication, correction, retraction, knockout, inhibitor, and loss-of-function evidence is eligible when it constrains a major claim.
Peer-reviewed primary studies are prioritized; systematic, scoping, and authoritative mechanistic reviews are eligible for terminology, study-family identification, and citation expansion.
Studies in humans, human tissue, mammalian cells, biochemical systems, and relevant animal models are eligible with organism, tissue, cell type, and assay context preserved.
Records in any language are eligible when an English title or abstract, accessible translation, or sufficient indexed metadata supports reliable screening and extraction.

queries.purpose: Recover the 2004 PARK8/LRRK2 cloning and mutation-discovery anchors plus early G2019S disease-association and founder reports; verify target aliases, author forms, and variant notation.
queries.query: (LRRK2[Title/Abstract] OR PARK8[Title/Abstract] OR dardarin[Title/Abstract]) AND (((Paisan-Ruiz C[Author] OR Zimprich A[Author]) AND ("2004/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2004/12/31"[Date - Publication])) OR ((Di Fonzo A[Author] OR Gilks WP[Author] OR Kachergus J[Author]) AND G2019S[Title/Abstract]))

queries.purpose: Recover early anchors linking Parkinson-associated variants to kinase, ROC GTPase, GTP-binding, and Ser1292-autophosphorylation mechanisms.
queries.query: (LRRK2[Title/Abstract] OR "leucine-rich repeat kinase 2"[Title/Abstract]) AND (((West AB[Author] AND "2005"[Date - Publication]) OR (Ito G[Author] AND "2007"[Date - Publication]) OR (Sheng Z[Author] AND "2012"[Date - Publication])) AND (kinase[Title/Abstract] OR GTPase[Title/Abstract] OR "GTP binding"[Title/Abstract] OR autophosphorylation[Title/Abstract]))

queries.purpose: Recover the phosphoproteomic Rab-substrate anchor and verify Rab-family names, phosphosite terminology, and follow-up physiological-validation vocabulary.

queries.query: (LRRK2[Title/Abstract]) AND (mutation*[Title/Abstract] OR G2019S[Title/Abstract] OR R1441C[Title/Abstract] OR R1441G[Title/Abstract] OR Y1699C[Title/Abstract] OR I2020T[Title/Abstract]) AND ("kinase activity"[Title/Abstract] OR GTPase[Title/Abstract] OR "GTP hydrolysis"[Title/Abstract]) AND (unchanged[Title/Abstract] OR decreased[Title/Abstract] OR variable[Title/Abstract] OR conflicting[Title/Abstract] OR independent[Title/Abstract] OR "loss of function"[Title/Abstract] OR knockout[Title/Abstract] OR inhibition[Title/Abstract] OR dispensable[Title/Abstract]) AND ("1900/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2024/12/31"[Date - Publication])

question_frame: Target-mechanism frame: From PubMed inception through 2024-12-31, in human Parkinson disease and relevant biochemical, cellular, animal, and human-tissue models, how was LRRK2 genetically discovered, which pathogenic, risk, and protective variants are supported, how do its ROC-COR GTPase and kinase activities regulate function, which endogenous substrates have physiological support, and which penetrance, ancestry, assay, tissue, species, replication, or contradictory findings limit causal strength and generality? Include primary genetic, biochemical, structural, phosphoproteomic, perturbational, and pathology evidence; use reviews for terminology and citation expansion.
stop_rules: Execute no more than the 12 preregistered PubMed query events.
Do not begin broad synthesis until q01, q02, and q03 recover their genetic, enzymatic, and Rab-substrate anchor families or the failed anchor and attempted alias expansion are documented.
Complete at least one focused confirmation event and one distinct challenge event for genetics, enzymatic mechanism, and physiological-substrate claims.
Complete both expansion events; stop expansion when q07 and q08 together add no new decision-relevant variant, substrate, physiological context, or limiting evidence.
Complete q12 and apply the 2024-12-31 cutoff after retrieval to resolve online-first, issue, and correction-date ambiguity.
Merge records through stable identifiers while preserving all query-to-record links; conflicting records sharing an identifier require adjudication before stopping.

Stop when every brief section has direct primary evidence, each high-impact claim has limiting or challenge evidence, and further PubMed retrieval is unlikely to change the strength assigned to a conclusion.
If the query budget is exhausted with an unresolved branch, stop and report the branch, missing anchor, and unavailable source class as a coverage gap.
